THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: A price ceiling sets a legal maximum price and is binding only when it lies below the market equilibrium price. A binding ceiling keeps price from rising to equilibrium, so quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied and a shortage develops. A ceiling at or above equilibrium is nonbinding because the market can still reach its equilibrium price.

transcript.sourceText: The market equilibrium is $30 and 200 units. A binding ceiling of $20 holds price below equilibrium; buyers demand 250 units while sellers supply 150. The resulting shortage is 250 - 150 = 100 units, so some willing buyers cannot purchase at the controlled price.
